questions.q: What is the planned build order for this capstone's five pieces?
options: Data Factory, then PowerShell, then HA/DR, then security, then Bicep
Security, then Bicep, then PowerShell, then HA/DR, then Data Factory
Bicep infrastructure, then security & compliance, then HA/DR, then PowerShell automation, then Data Factory ETL
All five pieces get built at the same time with no particular order
questions.explain: Each piece is a real dependency on the one before it: you need infrastructure before you can secure it, and a secured database before you replicate or automate it.

questions.q: Why does security and compliance come before HA/DR in this plan?
options: Security is less important so it can be done whenever
Replicating an unsecured database just produces two unsecured copies instead of one — encryption and access controls need to be in place before the database gets protected by failover
Azure requires security to be configured before any database can be created
HA/DR cannot technically be configured until security is enabled
questions.explain: HA/DR replicates the database as it exists at that point — building it after security means the failover group protects an already-secured database, not an unsecured one.

questions.q: Why is Data Factory ETL built last, in Chapter 6, rather than earlier?
options: Data Factory is the least important piece of the platform
It depends on a stable, secured, protected target database to write into — building it earlier means rebuilding it once the real infrastructure changes
Data Factory can only be built after a DR drill
There is no technical reason, it's arbitrary
questions.explain: The ETL feed needs somewhere stable to land data — that stability only exists once infrastructure, security, and HA/DR are already in place.

questions.q: What makes Chapter 7 different from Chapters 2 through 6?
options: It builds an entirely new, unrelated database
It repeats Chapter 2's Bicep work from scratch
It tests the finished platform under an unannounced DR drill and presents the results back to the same board that issued the mandate in Lesson 1
It is purely theoretical with no real deliverable
questions.explain: Chapter 7 proves the platform actually works under pressure and closes the loop with the leadership who asked for it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what would go wrong if HA/DR were built before security & compliance?
options: Nothing — the order genuinely doesn't matter
The failover group would replicate an unsecured database, meaning both the primary and the secondary copy would carry the same unresolved security gaps
Azure would reject the deployment outright
PowerShell automation would stop working
questions.explain: HA/DR's job is to replicate the current state of the database — if that state is unsecured, replication just doubles the exposure instead of fixing it.
